description: Requires a TechFabric engineer's Microsoft sign-in (scope blog.write). A read: what your agent needs to draft a Reddit post or thread answer in your own voice, from a published techfabric.com post or your own notes. The subreddit's rules, the frame (a plain title; first person; the problem, what you tried, what worked, your numbers), the disclosure line, the optional link last, a checklist and the steps to post it yourself. Send draft to check it: the site's writing rules plus Reddit's (no hashtags, no 'check out our', no call to action, substance before any link). No model is called and nothing is posted, voted or commented.

draft.description: The draft to check: the result then carries lint. Send it again after each rewrite until lint.ready is true

body.description: The post's body, as the engineer would paste it

title.description: The post's title (for an answer in a thread, leave it empty)

notes.description: The engineer's own notes about the problem, what they tried, what worked and their numbers (at most 8000 characters). Optional; send post, notes or both

post.description: A published post on techfabric.com the Reddit post draws on: its URL or its slug. Optional

subreddit.description: The subreddit the post or answer is for

thread.description: The Reddit thread being answered, if this is an answer: its URL. Optional

name: reddit_post_kit

founder_only.description: Set while Reddit posting is founder-only and the caller isn't the founder: tell the engineer, then help them draft notes for him

link.description: The article's link with the Reddit campaign, for the optional last line; null for a post from notes only

first_hand.description: The article's first-hand sentences, as published. The engineer may claim them only when the article is theirs (whose: yours); a colleague's are attributed to them

whose.description: Whose article it is: a colleague's first-hand experience is theirs, never the engineer's

title: Reddit kit for a post
